blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Wherever Jesus went, all kinds of people came close to listen. Some of them were the people everyone else stayed away from.

verses.text: Then drew near unto him all the publicans and sinners for to hear him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then drew near unto him all the publicans and sinners for to hear him.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Publicans were tax collectors who worked for Rome. Most people saw them as traitors and cheats. Sinners meant anyone known for living wrong. And Jesus did not keep them at a distance. He sat down and ate with them.

verses.text: And the Pharisees and scribes murmured, saying, This man receiveth sinners, and eateth with them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the Pharisees and scribes murmured, saying,

segments.speaker: pharisees
segments.text: This man receiveth sinners, and eateth with them.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The religious leaders meant it as a complaint. They could not understand why a teacher of God would sit at that table. So Jesus told them a story.

verses.text: And he spake this parable unto them, saying,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he spake this parable unto them, saying,

verses.text: What man of you, having an hundred sheep, if he lose one of them, doth not leave the ninety and nine in the wilderness, and go after that which is lost, until he find it?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: What man of you, having an hundred sheep, if he lose one of them, doth not leave the ninety and nine in the wilderness, and go after that which is lost, until he find it?

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: A hundred sheep is a lot of sheep to look after. Losing one might not seem like much. A careful businessman might say, ninety-nine is good enough. But a shepherd does not think that way. He knows each one.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: So he goes out. Over the rocks, through the brush, calling into the dark, until he hears that one small cry. It may take all night. The ninety-nine are safe together. The one alone is the one in danger, and the shepherd will not rest until it is found.

verses.text: And when he hath found it, he layeth it on his shoulders, rejoicing.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And when he hath found it, he layeth it on his shoulders, rejoicing.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: He does not scold the sheep. He does not make it walk home on its own. He picks it up and carries it across his shoulders, and he is glad the whole way back.

verses.text: And when he cometh home, he calleth together his friends and neighbours, saying unto them, Rejoice with me; for I have found my sheep which was lost.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And when he cometh home, he calleth together his friends and neighbours, saying unto them, Rejoice with me; for I have found my sheep which was lost.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: He cannot keep the joy to himself. He calls his friends and neighbors and throws a celebration for one lost sheep.

verses.text: I say unto you, that likewise joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine just persons, which need no repentance.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: I say unto you, that likewise joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine just persons, which need no repentance.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The people who were grumbling thought the ones at the table were too far gone. Jesus told them heaven sees it the other way. When one person who wandered off comes home, heaven does not shrug. Heaven rejoices.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: This is one of three stories Jesus told that day. A lost sheep, a lost coin, and a lost son. Each one ends the same way, with something found and a party thrown.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Some people hear this story and think of someone they love who has wandered off. Some people hear it and know they are the one that is lost. Either way, the story is clear about the shepherd. He does not wait for the sheep to find its own way back. He goes looking, and when he finds it, he carries it home with joy.

first_reader.note: Written by Claude in the landing session, then Claude's pastor and cultural read.

pastor.note: Faithful to Luke 15:1-7; the coin and the son named as the chapter's other two stories; no claim on who is lost tonight, only the shepherd's search.

cultural.note: Tax collectors and sinners shown as welcomed, not mocked; the grumblers answered, not scorned.
